headline: Wisla Plock narrow favourites; market move looks like noise
summary: The market makes Wisla Plock a narrow home favourite at 51.2% fair, with the draw at 24.8% and Radomiak at 24.0%. The fair handicap sits near -0.57 and the fair goals line at 2.96, with Under 3.0 still holding a slim majority at 51.2% and both teams to score unchanged at 60.3% on a thin seven-book consensus. The only movement on our tape is a single snapshot at 09:31 in which the sharp market, soft book B and soft book C all re-quoted, nudging Home by roughly two points while the consensus rose just 0.6. With 17.6 hours of history, five snapshots and only five books on the handicap, that is a routine morning re-quote rather than information.

voices.scout: And the sharp book bought Wisla by more than two points on the handicap, fair line sliding from minus 0.48 to minus 0.57. The consensus moved almost as far, so it isn't just one book. That's a real, if small, strengthening.
voices.sceptic: Hold on. All three moving books carry the same 09:31 timestamp, so you can't tell me who led. Only five books quote that handicap. And on the one-X-two, the consensus rose just 0.6 of a point while the sharp book moved two. That's one book's opinion, possibly a position adjustment, not informed money.
voices.gaffer: So the reading is simple. Wisla Plock narrow favourites at 51.2 per cent fair, draw 24.8, Radomiak 24.0, a fair handicap near minus 0.57 and a goals line of 2.96 with Under just ahead. All the movement is one 09:31 snapshot, about two points to the home side while the consensus barely moved. On five books and five snapshots, that's a morning re-quote, not a signal.
